page: Amazon Web Services i7i.12xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor, delivering 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations.

The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 11250 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a 28 Gbps baseline bandwidth. This combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage and fast DDR5 memory establishes a high-density resource profile for data-intensive operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance across several categories. The instance achieves a Passmark CPU score of 69056.45 and a database operations score of 26527.8, both placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are also strong, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4099.27 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at 72.52 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2137.69, and the lack of a dedicated GPU limits large-scale LLM text generation, which registers an average speed of 3.31 tokens per second for a 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.12xlarge offers a high ratio of local NVMe storage to memory, reducing the need for external network-attached storage for large datasets. This makes the instance highly suitable for workloads such as relational and non-relational databases, caching layers, data warehousing, and software compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.12xlarge is a storage-optimized server featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 11250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a 28 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show strong performance in database operations, memory bandwidth, and multi-threaded decompression, though single-core CPU performance and large-model LLM text generation remain average due to the lack of GPU acceleration. The high density of local NVMe storage and DDR5 memory provides qualitative cost efficiency by minimizing reliance on external block storage. This instance is designed for database hosting, caching layers, and software compilation workloads.
